summary: Robustness verification run for BNB-specific RSI parameters (rsi_oversold=25, rsi_overbought=60, hold_bars=168) tested across 54 WFA windows with FIXED parameters. Results show 61.1% positive Sharpe windows (below 70% target), aggregate OOS Sharpe 0.664 vs prior discovery 1.275 (-48% decline), confirming partial overfitting to original training window.

key_lessons.lesson: Fixed parameter robustness test exposes overfitting to original optimization window
key_lessons.specific_finding: When the discovered BNB parameters (rsi_oversold=25, rsi_overbought=60, hold_bars=168) were run across 54 fixed windows (no per-window optimization), Sharpe dropped from 1.275 to 0.664 (-48%). Only 61.1% of windows achieved positive Sharpe, below the 70% threshold.

key_lessons.lesson: 168 hold_bars (7-day mean reversion) works for BNB but regime sensitivity remains high
key_lessons.specific_finding: The longer hold_bars (168 bars = ~7 days at 1h) captures weekly mean reversion cycles in BNB's exchange token volatility profile. However, window-by-window performance varies dramatically (Sharpe range: -0.87 to 2.29), indicating strong regime dependency.

next_actions.action: Test shorter hold_bars (96-120 bars / 4-5 days) for more adaptive signal
next_actions.rationale: The 168-bar hold period may be too long, causing sensitivity to specific market regimes. Shorter holds could provide more consistent signals across varying market conditions.

next_actions.action: Implement regime filter to avoid trading in low-conviction market conditions
next_actions.rationale: Given 61.1% positive Sharpe windows and high variance, adding a volatility or trend regime filter could improve consistency by avoiding unfavorable market periods.

next_actions.action: Consider ensemble approach combining EMA Trend Gate with complementary signal types
next_actions.rationale: Pure mean-reversion shows marginal robustness. Combining with momentum or funding-rate signals could improve consistency across regimes.
